definition: A legal document that explains how an organization collects, uses, stores, and protects personal information from users or customers.
metaDescription: Learn what a privacy policy is and why it matters for your personal data protection. Understand how companies handle your information.
simpleExplanation: A privacy policy is like a contract between you and a company that tells you what they do with your personal information. It explains what data they collect, how they use it, who they share it with, and how you can control it.
whyItMatters: Privacy policies help you understand what happens to your personal data and make informed decisions about which services to use. They're legally required in many places and give you rights to control your information.
technicalDetail: Privacy policies typically include sections on data collection methods, legal basis for processing, retention periods, third-party sharing, international transfers, user rights (access, deletion, portability), security measures, and contact information for privacy inquiries.

examples.explanation: Facebook's privacy policy explains how they collect data from your posts, messages, and browsing activity, use it for targeted advertising, and share it with third-party app developers.
Amazon's privacy policy describes how they collect purchase history, payment information, and browsing data to personalize recommendations and process orders, and how long they keep this information.
A fitness app's privacy policy explains that it collects location data, health metrics, and device information to provide personalized workouts and may share anonymized data with research partners.
